thread:
alex: Heads up — we had ~40 scale-up launches in eu-west spot GPU pools between 02:30–04:30 UTC last night. Looks like autoscaler churn (binpack + AZ skew) + long GPU provision times. Can we audit flags and propose a safe canary?

Tess: saw it too. Pod startup p95 jumped from ~300ms -> ~1.2s for model-serving jobs. Queueing spiked, some requests timed out. GPU driver/warmup adds ~25-40s on cold nodes.

Sven: binpack is trying to consolidate which is normally good, but when spot availability differs across AZs it ends up requesting in the “wrong” AZ and we wait ages for instances. switching expander helps avoid cross-AZ thrash.

Maria: current cluster-autoscaler flags for gpux pools are pretty aggressive: `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m` and `--scale-down-delay-after-add=1m`. That nukes nodes before KV cache/warmup really pays off.

Ryan: note tradeoff: increasing unneeded-time raises idle cost. For a canary we can limit the change to just the gpux-eu-west nodepool to bound cost impact.

Alex: suggested canary config for gpux-eu-west:
```
--expander=priority
--scale-down-unneeded-time=30m
--scale-down-delay-after-add=15m
--max-node-provision-time=25m
```
Only apply to gpux-eu-west nodegroup via a patched configmap + annotation, roll to 1 pool, monitor 12h.

Tess: patch snippet I'll use (preview):
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cluster-autoscaler-params
data:
  CA_FLAGS: "--expander=priority --scale-down-unneeded-time=1800s --scale-down-delay-after-add=900s --max-node-provision-time=1500s"
```
I'll open PR and include rollout steps + rollback command.

deploy-bot: canary deploy requested by tess. Target: deployment/cluster-autoscaler (gpux-eu-west config). Rolling update queued.

infra-bot: metric alert: NodeProvisionTime[gpu][eu-west] spike at 03:14 UTC = 18m (normal baseline 6m). Linked issue: infra#4321.

Sven: also consider `--max-empty-bulk-delete=1` for gpu pools so we don't nuke leftover empty nodes in bulk while new nodes are still provisioning. And use the priority expander with node-group label priorities (lower numeric = higher priority).

Maria: I'll run a k-sim run comparing `binpack` vs `priority` for our mixture of short control-plane jobs + long-serving model pods and report EOD. Focus on: node churn, p95 pod start, KV cache hit rate, and cold-start tail.

Ryan: I'll run quick cost model for changing unneeded-time from 10m -> 30m for 1 pool (est. +$0.6/hr during idle windows) and add that to the canary PR.

Alex: monitoring checklist for canary: p95 pod start, NodeProvisionTime, number of scale-ups per hour, idle GPU-hours, and tail error rate. If node-provision-time > 20m or scale-ups/hr increases, revert.

Tess: I'll set up dashboards and PagerDuty threshold for NodeProvisionTime > 20m for gpux-eu-west. PR in ~30m.

Maria: FYI possible follow-up: evaluate `--scale-down-utilization-threshold` for gpu pools. Lowering it slightly keeps nodes longer when utilization is bursty.

Ryan: agreed. Also add `node.kubernetes.io/accelerator` labels into the priority decision so capacity is only drawn from compatible pools.

Alex: great. Action items: maria = sim + results, tess = config PR + dashboards + canary rollout, sven = coordinate priority labels + rollback plan, ryan = cost delta. We’ll reconvene after 12h of canary telemetry.

Sven: +1 :thumbsup: 

Tess: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/cluster-autoscaler/pulls/202 (includes flags + rollback steps)

deploy-bot: canary applied to nodepool/gpux-eu-west-1 at 04:10 UTC. Watch metrics.

infra-bot: tagging ticket infra#4321 with canary id 202-canary-gpux-eu-west

Ryan: verified alerting config added to the grafana board (shared link in PR). I'll post cost estimate in thread once done.

Maria: sim results: priority expander reduced cross-AZ provisioning events by ~60% in the trace, p95 pod-start improved ~180ms and KV cache hits increased. Uploading raw sim logs to PR.

Alex: thanks team — let’s let it run 12h and circle back. If all green, we schedule rollout to other EU zones next week.

Ops: ack, will keep P0 on-call loop informed.
notes: thread is a single Slack conversation about tuning cluster-autoscaler flags for GPU spot pools in eu-west. Messages are ordered chronologically and include bots and action items.
